mainTopic: Does the unattributed משנה about reading the מגילה early agree with רבי יוסי? Testing which early-reading case the משנה permits הספד and תענית on.
overview: Background: Earlier on the daf, רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי, who forbids fasting even on the day before a holiday listed in מגילת תענית. רבי יוחנן also ruled that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה. The גמרא tests a סתם משנה which says that villagers who read the מגילה early may still fast and eulogize on that day. It rules out the 14th, the 13th (יום ניקנור) and the 12th (יום טוריינוס), so it seems the משנה means the 11th, the day before a holiday, which goes against רבי יוסי. The גמרא answers that the משנה means the 12th, because יום טוריינוס was cancelled after שמעיה and אחיה were killed on it, as רב נחמן showed by decreeing a fast then. רב אשי adds that being the day before יום ניקנור is not enough to forbid it. The גמרא then tells the stories behind both days: the defeat of the Greek general ניקנור, and the downfall of טוריינוס after he killed לוליינוס and פפוס. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה. It records a dispute over how many fasts count as 'beginning' a series. It then rules that a fast falling on a festive day is kept until nightfall, like the חכמים. The chapter ends, and the new chapter's משנה lists emergencies that call for crying out at once: diseased crops, a forty-day break in the rain, rain that falls short for crops, trees or water storage, and a single city left without rain.

steps.title: The משנה: early reading days stay open for eulogy and fasting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of a סתם משנה: even on the day the מגילה is read early, הספד and תענית are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are permitted to eulogize and to fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the closing words of a משנה about people who read the מגילה before Purim. This line sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some villagers read the מגילה early, on the day the town gathers for market. The משנה says that reading it early does not turn that day into a holiday, so fasting and eulogies are still allowed. The גמרא will now test exactly which calendar day the משנה has in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: A eulogy; publicly mourning the dead

phrases.english: They are permitted in eulogizing and fasting.
phrases.notes: End of the משנה in מסכת מגילה about reading the מגילה early (on the 11th, 12th, or 13th of אדר).

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּתָּרִין בְּהֶסְפֵּד וְתַעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the סתם משנה that will be tested against רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי יוסי (from earlier on the daf).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An early reading day of the מגילה does not forbid הספד and תענית.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוחנן said the הלכה follows a סתם משנה. So whatever this משנה implies carries weight against his other ruling following רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Which case? First suggestion: walled cities reading on the 14th
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the משנה's permission applies. It first suggests walled-city residents (who normally read on the 15th) reading on the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? If you say it is about people who normally read on the fifteenth, and they read it on the fourteenth…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which exact case the משנה is talking about. It offers a first guess, which it will test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To know whether the משנה clashes with רבי יוסי, we need to pin down the calendar day. The first guess is a walled city (בני חמיסר) reading one day early, on the 14th. For a walled city, the 14th would normally be just a regular day.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a suggestion that will be tested
People of the fifteenth; residents of walled cities who read on the 15th

phrases.english: When?
phrases.notes: Asks for the precise case of the משנה.

phrases.english: If you say: people of the fifteenth
and they read it on the fourteenth,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case step 1's ruling covers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: On which calendar day does the משנה permit fasting despite an early reading?

steps.title: Rejecting the 14th: מגילת תענית forbids eulogy on both Purim days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion. מגילת תענית lists both the 14th and 15th as Purim days on which eulogizing is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really permitted? But it is written in מגילת תענית: the fourteenth day of it and the fifteenth day of it are days of Purim, on which one may not eulogize.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how fasting could be allowed on the 14th. It brings a source showing that the 14th and the 15th are both Purim days that forbid eulogizing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 14th is forbidden for eulogy, the משנה cannot be permitting eulogy there. On its own, though, someone might say the ban only covers each city's own Purim day. The next step closes that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it permitted? (a challenge: surely not!)
An ancient list of joyous dates on which fasting or eulogizing is forbidden

phrases.english: But is it permitted?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical challenge to the first suggestion.

phrases.english: But isn't it written in מגילת תענית:
The fourteenth day of it (אדר)
and the fifteenth day of it,
they are days of Purim
on which one may not eulogize.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָכְתִיב בִּמְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משנה means walled cities reading on the 14th.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מגילת תענית forbids eulogy on the 14th, so the משנה could not be permitting it there.

steps.title: רבא: each city is forbidden on the other city's Purim too
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that מגילת תענית adds the ban on both days to forbid walled cities on the 14th and unwalled cities on the 15th.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: it was needed only to forbid the people of this place on that day, and the people of that place on this day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא to show that the 14th is forbidden even for walled-city people. This completes the rejection of the first suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each city's own Purim is already a holiday from מגילת אסתר, so מגילת תענית had no need to repeat that. רבא says its added point is that both cities are forbidden on both days. So walled-city residents may not fast on the 14th, and the משנה cannot mean that case.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for; this rule's new point is…
Those of this place on this (other) day

phrases.english: And רבא said: it was only necessary

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לֶאֱסוֹר אֶת שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
phrases.english: to forbid those of this (walled city) on this (the 14th)
and those of this (unwalled town) on this (the 15th).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the קשיא of step 3 by showing the ban covers walled cities on the 14th.
steps.raayaObject: That the 14th is forbidden for fasting even for walled-city residents.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think each city is only barred from fasting on its own Purim. According to רבא, both the 14th and the 15th are forbidden for everyone.

steps.title: Second suggestion rejected: the 13th is יום ניקנור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא next suggests regular towns reading on the 13th. It rejects this because the 13th is יום ניקנור, a celebration day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it is about people of the fourteenth who read it on the thirteenth. But that is יום ניקנור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new case: unwalled towns reading one day early, on the 13th. It rejects the case right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 13th of אדר is יום ניקנור, the victory over the Greek general ניקנור, and it is listed in מגילת תענית. So fasting there is already forbidden on its own, and the משנה could not permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather; introduces a new attempt
People of the fourteenth; residents of unwalled towns
13th of אדר; celebrates the defeat of the Greek general ניקנור

phrases.english: But rather, people of the fourteenth
who read it on the thirteenth —
it is יום ניקנור!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, בְּנֵי אַרְבֵּיסַר וְקָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ בִּתְלֵיסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 14th fails, tries the 13th and knocks it down.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משנה means reading on the 13th.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 13th is itself a holiday in מגילת תענית, so fasting is forbidden there anyway.

steps.title: Third suggestion rejected: the 12th is יום טוריינוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reading on the 12th. It rejects this because the 12th is יום טוריינוס, also a celebration day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it is about people of the fourteenth who read it on the twelfth. But that is יום טוריינוס!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries reading two days early, on the 12th. This case is rejected the same way as the 13th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 12th of אדר is יום טוריינוס, which is also a joyous day in מגילת תענית. So the משנה's permission to fast cannot refer to the 12th either. Only the 11th is left.

keyTerms.meaning: 12th of אדר; a commemorative day in מגילת תענית connected to טוריינוס (Trajan)

phrases.english: But rather, people of the fourteenth
who read it on the twelfth —
it is יום טוריינוס!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, בְּנֵי אַרְבֵּיסַר וְקָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ בִּתְרֵיסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 5, now for the 12th.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משנה means reading on the 12th.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 12th is itself a holiday in מגילת תענית, so fasting is forbidden there anyway.

steps.title: The משנה must mean the 11th, which contradicts רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: By elimination, the משנה means reading on the 11th. It permits fasting there even though the 11th is the day before יום טוריינוס, which goes against רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that they read it on the eleventh, and the משנה teaches that eulogizing and fasting are permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the משנה must mean the 11th. This sharpens the challenge: the משנה permits fasting on the day before a holiday, which רבי יוסי forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 11th is the day right before יום טוריינוס. רבי יוסי forbids fasting on the day before such a holiday, but this סתם משנה allows it. Since רבי יוחנן ruled like both רבי יוסי and the סתם משנה, his two rulings now seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not…? (introduces the only remaining option)

steps.whatToRemember: The 14th and 15th are Purim, the 13th is יום ניקנור, and the 12th is יום טוריינוס. So the משנה's 'permitted to fast' must mean the 11th, the day before a holiday. That disagrees with רבי יוסי and creates a contradiction in רבי יוחנן's rulings.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו, דְּקָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ בַּחֲדֵיסַר,
phrases.english: Rather, is it not where they read it on the eleventh,
and it teaches: permitted in eulogizing and fasting!
phrases.notes: Even though the 11th is the day before יום טוריינוס, against רבי יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, דְּקָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ בַּחֲדֵיסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With every other date ruled out, lands on the 11th and draws the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's two rulings: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, and the הלכה follows a סתם משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סתם משנה permits fasting on the day before a holiday, while רבי יוסי forbids it. Both cannot be the הלכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's coming resolution of רבי יוחנן's apparent contradiction about fasting on the day before a holiday in מגילת תענית.

steps.title: The משנה means people who normally read on the 14th but read on the 12th
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its reading: the משנה refers to people who usually read on the 14th but read on the 12th this year. יום טוריינוס is no obstacle, since it was cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The משנה is talking about people who normally read on the 14th, but read the מגילה on the 12th. And as for what you said, that the 12th is יום טוריינוס: יום טוריינוס itself was cancelled, because שמעיה and his brother אחיה were killed on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the 'elimination' conclusion from Step 7 and offers a new reading of the משנה. It then removes the problem of יום טוריינוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 ruled out the 12th because it was יום טוריינוס, a celebration day. Now the גמרא says that holiday is no longer in force: the day turned sad when שמעיה and אחיה were killed. With no holiday on the 12th, the משנה can permit fasting then. It no longer has to mean the 11th, so it does not clash with רבי יוסי about the day before יום טוריינוס. Step 10 will raise one more problem with the 12th.

keyTerms.meaning: People who normally read the מגילה on the 14th (unwalled towns)
Two brothers killed on the 12th of אדר, which caused the holiday to be cancelled

steps.confusionAlert: The 12th is not the day before יום טוריינוס. It IS יום טוריינוס. The point is that this holiday itself no longer exists.

phrases.english: No, it refers to those who normally read on the fourteenth,
but who read it on the twelfth.
And as for what you said, that it is Trajan's Day:
Trajan's Day itself was annulled,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְנֶהֶרְגוּ בּוֹ שְׁמַעְיָה וַאֲחִיָּה אֶחָיו.
phrases.english: since Shemaya and his brother Achiya were killed on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בְּנֵי אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, וְקָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ בִּתְרֵיסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attack in Step 7 by going back to the 12th and removing the reason it was rejected in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the case plus removal of the objection (the holiday was cancelled)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 12th is יום טוריינוס, so the משנה could not permit fasting on it.
steps.terutzMaskana: יום טוריינוס was cancelled, so fasting on the 12th is allowed and the משנה means the 12th.

steps.title: Proof from רב נחמן decreeing a fast on the 12th
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן declared a fast on the 12th. When the רבנן objected that it was יום טוריינוס, he answered that the holiday had been cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case where רב נחמן declared a fast on the 12th. The רבנן said to him: 'It is יום טוריינוס!' He told them: 'יום טוריינוס itself was cancelled, because שמעיה and his brother אחיה were killed on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a real case. רב נחמן actually set a fast on the 12th for this same reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim that יום טוריינוס was cancelled is not just theory. An אמורא relied on it in practice and defended it against the רבנן's objection, using the exact same reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who set a fast on the 12th

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא בִּתְרֵיסַר,
phrases.english: As in the case when Rav Nachman decreed a fast on the twelfth,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: יוֹם טוּרְיָינוֹס הוּא!
phrases.english: the Sages said to him: It is Trajan's Day!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: יוֹם טוּרְיָינוֹס גּוּפֵיהּ בַּטּוֹלֵי בַּטְּלוּהּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: Trajan's Day itself was annulled,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְנֶהֶרְגוּ בּוֹ שְׁמַעְיָה וַאֲחִיָּה אָחִיו.
phrases.english: since Shemaya and his brother Achiya were killed on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא בִּתְרֵיסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 8's claim that יום טוריינוס was cancelled.
steps.raayaObject: That יום טוריינוס was cancelled and fasting on the 12th is allowed
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's actual decree of a fast on the 12th, and his reply to the רבנן

steps.title: But the 12th is the day before יום ניקנור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even if יום טוריינוס is cancelled, the 12th should still be forbidden as the day before יום ניקנור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you should get the ban from a different source: the 12th is the day before יום ניקנור (the 13th)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with fasting on the 12th. It is the day right before יום ניקנור, which is still celebrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, one may not fast on the day before a celebration day. Even with יום טוריינוס gone, the 12th sits right before the 13th, יום ניקנור, so fasting should still be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it instead from (another reason)

phrases.english: But let him derive it instead
from the fact that it is the day before Nicanor's Day!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ יוֹם שֶׁלִּפְנֵי נִיקָנוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of Steps 8-9 from a different direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that fasting on the 12th is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי forbids fasting on the day before a celebration day, and the 12th comes right before יום ניקנור.

steps.title: רב אשי: No extra ban because of the next day
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers: the holiday on the 12th itself was cancelled, so we would not make a new ban on the 12th just because it comes before יום ניקנור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Now that the holiday on this day itself was cancelled, should we go and make a decree against fasting because of יום ניקנור?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from Step 10 with a rhetorical question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 12th's own holiday was cancelled, it would make no sense to keep the day restricted only because it is next to another holiday. The 'day before' ban is weaker than the day's own holiday, so it does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: A late אמורא who gives the answer
Now, since (introduces a 'how much more so' style argument)

steps.whatToRemember: The 12th of אדר may be a fast day: יום טוריינוס was cancelled, and being the day before יום ניקנור is not enough to forbid it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Now that they annulled the day itself,
shall we arise and decree because of Nicanor's Day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַשְׁתָּא אִיהוּ גּוּפֵיהּ בַּטְּלוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reasoning (we do not add a secondary restriction when the main one was removed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 12th should be forbidden as the day before יום ניקנור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the 12th's own holiday was cancelled, no ban is made because of the next day.

steps.title: What are יום ניקנור and יום טוריינוס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the historical background of the two holidays it has been discussing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is ניקנור, and what is טוריינוס?
steps.whatsHappening: The legal discussion is finished. Now the גמרא asks what these two holidays actually celebrated, which sets up the stories that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not a challenge. It asks for background information, so the reader understands what each date commemorates.

phrases.english: What is Nicanor and what is Trajan?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נִיקָנוֹר וּמַאי טוּרְיָינוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from law to the history behind the holidays mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The origin of יום ניקנור and יום טוריינוס

steps.title: The story of ניקנור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that ניקנור, a Greek general, threatened ירושלים every day. When the חשמונאים defeated him, they cut off his thumbs and big toes and hung them on the city gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: ניקנור was one of the Greek generals. Every day he would wave his hand over יהודה and ירושלים and say, 'When will it fall into my hands so I can trample it?' When the kingdom of the חשמונאים grew strong and defeated them, they cut off his thumbs and big toes and hung them on the gates of ירושלים. They said: 'The mouth that spoke with arrogance, and the hands that waved over ירושלים, let revenge be taken on them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first half of the question, explaining why the 13th of אדר became a celebration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ניקנור boasted with his mouth and threatened with his hands. His punishment matched his crime: his thumbs and big toes were cut off and put on public display at the very city he had threatened.

keyTerms.meaning: Waved his hand (in a threatening way)

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: נִיקָנוֹר, אֶחָד מֵאִפַּרְכֵי יְוָונִים הָיָה,
phrases.english: As it is taught: Nicanor was one of the Greek generals,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם הָיָה מֵנִיף יָדוֹ
phrases.english: and each and every day he would wave his hand
over Judea and Jerusalem, and say:
When will it fall into my hands so I may trample it?
And when the Hasmonean kingdom grew strong and defeated them,
they cut off his thumbs and big toes
and hung them on the gates of Jerusalem, and said:
The mouth that spoke with arrogance,
and the hands that waved over Jerusalem:
let vengeance be taken on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: נִיקָנוֹר, אֶחָד מֵאִפַּרְכֵי יְוָונִים הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of Step 12's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יום ניקנור celebrates the Hasmonean victory over the Greek general ניקנור.

steps.title: The story of טוריינוס begins
steps.stepSummary: טוריינוס wanted to kill the brothers לוליינוס and פפוס and mocked them, asking why their God would not save them as He saved חנניה, מישאל and עזריה. They answered that those three were perfect צדיקים, and נבוכדנצר was a fitting king for a miracle to happen through.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is טוריינוס? They said: When טוריינוס wanted to kill לוליינוס and his brother פפוס in Laodicea, he said to them: 'If you are from the nation of חנניה, מישאל and עזריה, let your God come and save you from my hand, the way He saved חנניה, מישאל and עזריה from the hand of נבוכדנצר!' They said to him: 'חנניה, מישאל and עזריה were perfect צדיקים, and they deserved to have a miracle done for them. And נבוכדנצר was a proper king, and it was fitting for a miracle to be done through him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the second half of the question by telling the story behind יום טוריינוס. The story continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טוריינוס mocks the brothers by comparing them to חנניה, מישאל and עזריה. They answer humbly: a miracle requires both perfect צדיקים and a legitimate king, so they should not expect one. Their reply continues in steps 15 and 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Two brothers, Jewish leaders, whom טוריינוס wanted to kill
The three saved from the fiery furnace of נבוכדנצר

phrases.english: What is Trajan? They said:
When Trajan sought to kill
Luleyanus and his brother Pappas in Laodicea,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: אִם מֵעַמּוֹ שֶׁל חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה אַתֶּם —
phrases.english: he said to them: If you are from the nation of Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
let your God come and save you from my hand,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהִצִּיל אֶת חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: just as He saved Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah
from the hand of Nebuchadnezzar!
They said to him: Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah
were completely righteous,
and they were worthy of having a miracle performed for them.
And Nebuchadnezzar was a legitimate king,
and it was fitting for a miracle to be performed through him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טוּרְיָינוֹס? אָמְרוּ: כְּשֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ טוּרְיָינוֹס לַהֲרוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of Step 12's question. The story continues next.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Begins the account of טוריינוס's attempt to kill לוליינוס and פפוס, which is the background of יום טוריינוס.

steps.title: טוריינוס is too lowly for a miracle
steps.stepSummary: The brothers finish their contrast: נבוכדנצר was a real king, but טוריינוס is a commoner, so no miracle will happen through him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that wicked man is a commoner, and it is not fitting for a miracle to be done through him.
steps.whatsHappening: The brothers finish answering טוריינוס's mocking question. They explain the second difference between their case and the story of חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 they said two things made the old miracle fitting: perfect צדיקים, and a real king, נבוכדנצר. Here they say the second condition is missing too, because טוריינוס is only a הדיוט. A miracle is a public display of ה׳'s power, and he is not important enough for one.

keyTerms.meaning: commoner, an ordinary person, not a true king

phrases.english: And that wicked one is a commoner,
phrases.notes: Contrast with נבוכדנצר, who was a real king.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לַעֲשׂוֹת נֵס עַל יָדוֹ.
phrases.english: and it is not fitting to do a miracle through him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע, הֶדְיוֹט הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part contrast begun in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No miracle is expected, because טוריינוס is not a fitting king for one.

steps.title: Our death is from our sins, and ה׳ will avenge us
steps.stepSummary: The brothers say they deserve death from ה׳ for their sins, and ה׳ has many ways to carry it out. He placed them in טוריינוס's hands only so that He can later punish him for their blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have become liable for destruction before ה׳. If you do not kill us, ה׳ has many other killers, and many bears and lions in His world that could attack and kill us. Rather, ה׳ gave us into your hands only so that in the future He will take payment for our blood from you.
steps.whatsHappening: The brothers turn the mockery around. They are not dying because ה׳ is weak. They are dying because of their own sins, and טוריינוס will be punished for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They accept that they themselves are not perfect צדיקים and deserve כליה‎. ה׳ has many messengers who could carry this out, so the fact that טוריינוס is the one doing it is a sign against him. The killer will have to pay for their blood.

keyTerms.meaning: to collect payment, to take revenge

steps.confusionAlert: They are not saying טוריינוס is innocent because they deserved to die. The opposite is true: even though they deserved death, he is still guilty for being the one who chose to kill them.

phrases.english: And we have become liable for destruction before the Omnipresent,
and if you do not kill us —
the Omnipresent has many killers,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַרְבֵּה דּוּבִּין וַאֲרָיוֹת יֵשׁ לוֹ לַמָּקוֹם בְּעוֹלָמוֹ
phrases.english: and the Omnipresent has many bears and lions in His world
that could attack us and kill us.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, לֹא מְסָרָנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּיָדְךָ,
phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave us into your hands
only so that He will in the future exact our blood from you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָנוּ נִתְחַיַּיבְנוּ כְּלָיָה לַמָּקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 'not perfect צדיקים' half of their answer and turns it into a warning to טוריינוס.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They die for their own sins, and their killer will be punished.

steps.title: טוריינוס kills them and is killed himself
steps.stepSummary: טוריינוס kills the brothers right away. Before people even left the spot, officials from Rome arrived and smashed his skull with clubs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, he killed them immediately. They said: they had not moved from there before officials came from Rome and split his skull with clubs.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The brothers' warning comes true almost immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quick punishment shows that what the brothers said was true: ה׳ took payment for their blood from טוריינוס. This is why the day became a celebration, יום טוריינוס, which the גמרא was discussing in the earlier steps.
steps.whatToRemember: יום טוריינוס celebrates the downfall of טוריינוס, who killed לוליינוס and פפוס and was struck down right afterward.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the historical source of יום טוריינוס, the holiday discussed in steps 6, 8 and 9, closing the side discussion.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הֲרָגָן מִיָּד.
phrases.english: Even so, he killed them immediately.
They said: they had not moved from there
until two officials came from Rome
and split his skull with clubs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הֲרָגָן מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the outcome of the brothers' warning.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: טוריינוס was punished right away, and his downfall became the holiday יום טוריינוס.

steps.title: How many fasts count as having started?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about not starting fasts on Thursday or on ראש חודש. It then asks how many fasts must already have been kept for the series to count as 'begun', so that it is not interrupted for a festive day.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We do not decree a public fast starting on a Thursday…', 'We do not decree a fast on ראש חודש…'. And how many fasts make a 'beginning'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story and goes back to the משנה. It quotes the משנה as a setup, then asks a clarifying question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says not to decree fasts on festive days like ראש חודש, but if a series of fasts already began, you do not interrupt it. The גמרא wants a definition: how many fasts must already be done before it counts as 'begun'?

keyTerms.meaning: New Moons, the start of each month

phrases.english: We do not decree a fast on the community
starting on a Thursday, etc.,
phrases.notes: So that people buying food for שבת right after a fast will not make prices rise.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין גּוֹזְרִין תַּעֲנִית בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: We do not decree a fast on New Moons, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' includes the משנה's rule that once fasts began, they are not interrupted.

phrases.english: And how many is a 'beginning'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה הָוְיָא הַתְחָלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum number of fasts already kept for a series to count as 'begun'.

steps.title: Three fasts or one fast
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא says three fasts make a beginning. רבי אסי says even one fast is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא said: three. רבי אסי said: one.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אחא, the series is only 'begun' once three fasts have been kept before the festive day. According to רבי אסי, even one fast before it means the series has begun, so it continues through the festive day. The גמרא leaves the disagreement here without deciding.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa said: three.
Rabbi Asi said: one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא אָמַר: שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אחא: three fasts. רבי אסי: one fast.

steps.title: The משנה's rule is only רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that the משנה's rule (when a fast falls on a festive day, you fast but do not complete it until night) is the view of רבי מאיר in the name of רבן גמליאל. The חכמים say you fast and complete the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is the view of רבי מאיר, who said it in the name of רבן גמליאל. But the חכמים say: one fasts and completes the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: רב tells us whose opinion the משנה's rule is, and that the חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that even when a series of fasts continues onto a festive day, you do not finish that fast until nightfall. רב says this is only רבי מאיר's report of רבן גמליאל. The חכמים hold that once the series continues, you fast the full day, even on a festive day.

keyTerms.meaning: he completes the fast until nightfall

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the series of fasts continues onto the festive day. They only argue about whether that day's fast lasts until nightfall.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir
who said it in the name of Rabban Gamliel,
but the Rabbis say: one fasts and completes the fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new point on the same משנה, this time about completing the fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not completing the fast is רבי מאיר's view in the name of רבן גמליאל. The חכמים say you fast and complete it.

steps.title: The הלכה: fast and complete
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא taught in the name of רב הונא that the הלכה is like the חכמים: you fast the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught in the name of רב הונא: the הלכה is that one fasts and completes the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the disagreement from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the two views in step 20, the הלכה follows the חכמים. If a series of public fasts runs onto a festive day, that day's fast is kept until nightfall.
steps.whatToRemember: A series of fasts that has begun is not interrupted for a festive day, and the הלכה is that you fast the full day (like the חכמים).

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra taught in the name of Rav Huna:
The halakha is: one fasts and completes the fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה מִתְעַנֶּה וּמַשְׁלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the disagreement from step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows the חכמים: one fasts and completes the fast.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter סדר תעניות כיצד
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing formula for the chapter סדר תעניות כיצד.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'סדר תעניות כיצד'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the closing line that marks the end of the chapter we have been learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן expresses the hope that we will come back and learn this chapter again. Everything after this line belongs to a new chapter.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The formula said when a chapter is finished.
'How is the order of fasts done?' The name of the chapter now ending.

steps.whatToRemember: The second chapter is now finished. The new chapter's opening משנה refers back to the gradual order of fasts taught in the first chapter.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
'How is the order of fasts done'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter right after the final הלכה in step 21 (you fast the whole day).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter סדר תעניות כיצד is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: The slow order of fasts is only for a late first rain
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה limits the gradual order of fasts to a delay of the first rain. Diseased crops and a forty-day break in the rain call for crying out immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: This order of fasts that we learned applies when the first rainfall is late. But if crops changed (became diseased), we cry out about it right away. Likewise, if the rain stopped for forty days between one rainfall and the next, we cry out, because that is a plague of drought.
steps.whatsHappening: The third chapter opens with a new משנה. It says the step-by-step fasting order from before is only for one situation, and some emergencies skip straight to crying out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first chapter built a slow, gradual system: first individuals fast, then the community, with more and more severity. This משנה says that system is meant only for a late רביעה ראשונה. When damage is already happening, such as sick crops or a long dry break after the rains began, there is no time to wait, so מתריעין happens immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: The first rainfall of the season.
Crops that changed, meaning they became diseased or blighted.
They cry out, raising an alarm through prayer and blasts.

steps.confusionAlert: Here שֶׁשָּׁנוּ comes from שינוי, meaning 'that changed'. It does NOT mean 'that we learned' (from שנה, to learn). The phrase describes crops whose look changed because of disease.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the theme for the whole chapter: which disasters are urgent enough to skip the gradual fasting order.

phrases.english: This order of fasts
is stated for (a delay in) the first rainfall.
But crops that changed (became diseased) —
we cry out over them immediately.
And likewise, if the rains stopped
for forty days between one rain and the next —
we cry out over them,
because it is a plague of drought.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵדֶר תַּעֲנִיּוֹת אֵלּוּ הָאָמוּר בִּרְבִיעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן. It refers back to the fasting order taught in the earlier chapters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gradual fasting order is only for a late first rain. Diseased crops and a forty-day gap in the rain require crying out immediately.

steps.title: Rain that was not enough for every need: cry out right away
steps.stepSummary: If rain helped crops but not trees, trees but not crops, or both but did not fill the water storage, we cry out immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: If rain fell enough for the crops but not for the trees, or for the trees but not for the crops, or for both but not enough to fill the cisterns, ditches, and caves, we cry out about it right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of emergencies. Here it covers cases where rain came, but not enough for all the needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some rain falling does not mean the danger is over. Crops, trees, and stored drinking water each need a different amount of rain. A shortage in any one of them is a real threat, so it also gets an immediate response.

keyTerms.meaning: Long ditches or trenches for holding water.

phrases.english: If (rains) fell enough for the crops
but did not fall enough for the trees,
(or) for the trees but not for the crops,
(or) for both this and that
but not (enough) for the cisterns, ditches, and caves —
we cry out over them immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָרְדוּ לַצְּמָחִין אֲבָל לֹא יָרְדוּ לָאִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more emergency cases to the list started in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain that falls short for crops, trees, or water storage requires crying out immediately.

steps.title: A single city without rain, supported by a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A city that alone received no rain is also a reason to cry out. The משנה brings a פסוק from עמוס showing this is a sign from heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, a city that rain did not fall on, as it is written: 'And I caused it to rain on one city, and on another city I did not cause it to rain; one portion was rained on…'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last emergency case, one city that stayed dry while others got rain. It backs this up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the region as a whole had rain, so this is not a general drought. The פסוק in עמוס shows that rain falling on one city and skipping another is a deliberate punishment. That is why such a city must cry out.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written, introducing a פסוק.
And I caused it to rain.

steps.whatToRemember: The opening משנה of this chapter lists emergencies that skip the slow fasting order and call for crying out at once: diseased crops, a forty-day gap in the rain, rain that falls short for any need, and one city left without rain.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן עִיר שֶׁלֹּא יָרְדוּ עָלֶיהָ גְּשָׁמִים,
phrases.english: And likewise, a city on which rains did not fall,
as it is written: 'And I caused it to rain on one city'
'and on another city I did not cause it to rain;'
'one portion was rained on, etc.'
phrases.notes: עמוס ד:ז. The verse continues: the portion that got no rain withered.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן עִיר שֶׁלֹּא יָרְדוּ עָלֶיהָ גְּשָׁמִים דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final case to the משנה's list and supports it with a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single city that did not receive rain must cry out. The פסוק shows this is a targeted punishment from heaven.
